claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 11 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he doesn't live with you, are you contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be (or the equivalent in kind) towards his upkeep - such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions to make sure I have all the information:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. One final question:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any special living arrangements (such as living with someone else, or in residential accommodation), or does he live with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, he's been in hospital for a while now - about 3 or 4 months I think it's been.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. This is an important detail. I have a couple of follow-up questions about Alex's hospital stay:

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital - for example, on things like clothes, toys, treats, or other items for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I want to help him, but it's been difficult with everything going on. I haven't really been keeping track of whether I'm spending regularly on him or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it's a difficult situation and these details can be hard to keep track of during such a challenging time.

Let me ask one more question to help clarify:

**Over the past few months while Alex has been in hospital, have you been buying him things like clothes, toiletries, books, games, treats, or other items - even if it's just occasionally? Or have you not been able to spend money on him during this time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I really can't say for certain. It's been such a difficult time and I honestly haven't kept track of whether I've been spending on those things regularly or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - this is a very difficult situation and it's understandable that you haven't been keeping track of these details during such a challenging time.

Based on the information you've provided, let me summarize what we know:

- Alex is 11 years old
- You live in the UK
- Alex normally lives with you
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- Alex has been in hospital for approximately 3-4 months
- You're uncertain about whether you've been regularly spending money on him during his hospital stay

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child is in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you're usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit unless you regularly spend money on them. Since Alex has been in hospital for 3-4 months (which exceeds 12 weeks), and you're uncertain about whether you've been regularly spending money on him, I don't have sufficient information to make a definite assessment of your current eligibility.

You would have initially been eligible for Child Benefit when Alex was living at home with you. However, the question of whether you can continue to receive it now depends on details about your spending on Alex that you understandably don't have clear information about.

I'd recommend contacting HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly - they can review your specific circumstances in detail and help you understand your entitlement during this period.

conversation.text: I hope this information is helpful, even though I cannot give you a definite answer. HMRC will be able to look at your specific situation and help you understand your options. I wish Alex a speedy recovery.
